rebuttal_or_critique: I find the arguments for a pause premature. With headline CPI at 7.44% and food inflation at 11.51%, we are witnessing a significant breach of our tolerance band that risks unanchoring inflation expectations. While my colleagues point to core inflation at 4.90% as a reason for comfort, history shows that supply-side shocks in food and fuel often permeate into generalized inflation if not met with a firm monetary response. A positive output gap of 0.60% alongside resilient GVA growth of 7.80% suggests that the economy can absorb further tightening. Relying on the hope that food shocks are merely transient is a luxury we cannot afford when the mandate is to ensure durable price stability. We must act to prevent the current inflation trajectory from becoming entrenched.
